metadata.methods_description: EEG was recorded using a g.tec Nautilus wireless system with 16 electrodes positioned over sensorimotor cortex (10-10 system: Fz, FC3, FC2, FCz, FC4, C3, C1, Cz, C2, C4, CP3, CP1, CPz, CP2, CP4) at 500 Hz sampling rate with 0.1-100 Hz bandpass filtering. Tendon vibration was delivered via wireless electromechanical vibrators (Vibramoov) placed on distal biceps and triceps tendons of the left arm. Stimulation consisted of three-second sequences with 1-second linear ramps and 1-second stable frequency intervals. Each participant completed three blocks of 72 vibrations (36 illusion, 36 control) with randomized inter-stimulus intervals (1-3 seconds).

funding.funder_name: This work was supported by the Fondation CHUV, Lausanne, Switzerland; the Loterie Romande, Lausanne, Switzerland; and Techno Concept, Mane, France.

funding.award_title: Disentangling the percepts of illusory movement and sensory stimulation during tendon vibration in the EEG
